purpose: Elosulfase alfa is used to treat a rare genetic condition called Morquio A syndrome (also known as Mucopolysaccharidosis type IVA or MPS IVA). In this condition, your body is missing an important enzyme that breaks down certain sugars, causing them to build up and damage your bones, joints, and organs. This medicine helps replace the missing enzyme so your body can work more normally.
how_it_works: Your body normally makes an enzyme called N-acetylgalactosamine-6-sulfatase, which breaks down certain complex sugars. In Morquio A syndrome, this enzyme is missing or does not work properly, causing sugar buildup that damages your body over time. Elosulfase alfa is a man-made version of this enzyme given through an IV infusion, helping your body clear out those harmful sugar buildups.
common_side_effects: Fever, chills, headache, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, tiredness, and mild allergic reactions during or shortly after the infusion such as rash, flushing, or itching are the most common side effects.
warnings: Serious and life-threatening allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) can happen during infusions, so you will always be monitored closely by healthcare staff. Tell your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing, chest tightness, severe skin reactions, or feel faint. Because breathing problems can worsen with the infusion, patients with respiratory issues need extra caution. You should also let your doctor know about all your medications and any past reactions.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 2 mg per kilogram of your body weight, given as an intravenous (IV) infusion once every week. The infusion is done in a clinic or hospital setting and typically takes several hours. Your doctor will determine the exact schedule and infusion rate based on how you tolerate the treatment.
